Built into the app: the MovieBox catalog, direct playback and subtitles. No server or account needed.
Your own Cinemacore server. Probed at launch; falls back to the demo catalog if it does not answer.
TMDB catalog with the provider’s web player. Works without setup; no offline downloads.
Offline sample catalog for browsing the interface.

The default source. The app talks to MovieBox directly from this device, so there is no gateway or desktop server to start. A connection is required for browsing and streaming; downloads are supported for direct files.
Your own Cinemacore server (go run ./cmd/cinemacore). It is probed at launch; if it does not answer, the bundled demo catalog is used and labelled as such.
Catalog data comes from TMDB and playback opens the provider’s web player inside the app. Downloads and offline playback are not available on this source.
Bundled sample catalog for offline browsing and interface checks. No requests leave the device.
From a phone use your computer’s LAN address. 127.0.0.1 means the phone itself; the Android emulator reaches the host at 10.0.2.2. Leave blank to use the build default.

Your key overrides the build or environment key, which overrides StreamHype’s published fallback. StreamHype works with no key at all; a personal key simply uses your own TMDB quota. The key is stored on this device only.
Start the next episode automatically when the current one ends.
Applied to new playback and remembered on this device.
Resume points and recently watched titles.
Choose which Home rails appear and in what order.
How the app works, gateway setup and playback notes.
Inspect the active catalog and preview app dialogs.
How the app works, how to connect a gateway, and what playback can do.
Home shows rails from the active catalog. Tap a poster for details, episodes, cast and available languages. Search matches titles and genres.
Playback position is saved while you watch. History keeps the last point for each episode so you can continue where you stopped.

The app resolves one catalog at launch. Settings shows the resolved source and whether it is live or a demo fallback. A gateway that does not answer falls back to the bundled demo catalog so browsing still works.
Choose Gateway server, enter the base URL, then Apply and reconnect. On the emulator the host machine is 10.0.2.2; on a phone use the computer’s LAN address, not 127.0.0.1.
When the gateway will not connect

Confirm the server is running (go run ./cmd/cinemacore), that both devices share a network, and that no firewall blocks port 8080. Lab can probe the gateway version and show what the app actually reached. Local http gateways are supported.
The provider returns one stream with several quality labels. Choosing a quality re-prepares ExoPlayer at the same position; it is not a second download.
Tracks arrive as WebVTT or SRT and are cached in the app’s cache folder. Media3 renders both: SRT is handed over with the correct MIME type, so no separate conversion step is needed.
Playback is handled by Media3 ExoPlayer. Progressive MP4, HLS and DASH are supported; codec support still depends on the device, so an unusual audio track may need another rendition.

Only direct progressive files can be downloaded. HLS and DASH streams are refused with an explanation because they are segmented. There is no storage cap and no automatic deletion. Completed files play from the app’s data folder, and StreamHype web titles cannot be downloaded.

Watchlist, history, resume points, preferences and the download queue are stored as JSON in the app’s private data folder. Catalog, poster, playback and subtitle requests go to the source you selected; your library is not uploaded anywhere.
A TMDB key you enter is stored with the other settings. Gateway requests go to the URL you configure; StreamHype catalog requests go to TMDB. The app has no analytics or advertising SDK.
Clearing app storage or uninstalling removes settings, history and downloads together. There is no account, so there is nothing to sign out of.
Diagnostics for the active catalog and previews of the app’s blocking dialogs.
These dialogs normally appear only when the gateway demands them. Previews are local: they make no request and change no app state.

The gateway refused this region or device. The real gate offers no retry because the answer is not transient. If you use a VPN, reconnect to a supported region and open the app again.
This build is older than the minimum the gateway supports. The real gate blocks playback until Cinemacore is updated and offers no way to continue.
Version 0.2.0 is available. The real prompt is dismissible, so you can keep watching and update when convenient.
